newsitem.title: CHINA: French president to open trade fair in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: French president to open trade fair in Shanghai.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will open a trade fair showcasing more than 300 French companies during a trip in May to Shanghai, once known as the Paris of the East, Foreign Trade Minister Yves Galland said on Wednesday.
Dates for Chirac's state visit to China have yet to be confirmed, but the Shanghai leg would coincide with the May 17-21 France '97 exhibition, French sources said.
Gallard told reporters the trade show would be the largest gathering of French companies in China, with around 50 percent of the exhibitors making their Chinese debut.
It would also be the first such show in more than 10 years to be inaugurated by a French president, he said.
Around 75 percent of the exhibitors would be small and medium-sized companies, reflecting a trend in France towards exports and foreign investment, Gallard said.
Sectors represented would include telecommunications, energy, investment, technology transfer, collaboration in machinery, plastics, electronics and automated production, Gallard said.

France is the third-biggest European investor in China after Germany and the United Kingdom, with actual inflow of French capital by the end of September 1996 totalling $1.3 billion, the official Chinese media has reported.

During the first nine months of 1996, French investors signed 146 contracts involving $1 billion in pledged capital, more than double the amount pledged in the same period in 1995, according to the China Daily.
The newspaper said on Tuesday that France is a crucial supplier of technology to China, with Chinese imports of French technology between 1980 and 1996 valued at $6.8 billion.
Galland said high-tech French companies that already have a strong presence in China would be confirming their presence in the country at the France '97 exhibition.

More than 10 major French banks and insurance companies would also attend, with a strong contingent of engineering companies that are eager to get involved in Shanghai's booming construction industry.

Shanghai, China's biggest city with a population of around 13 million people, is the country's economic heart. City fathers have said they are keen to reclaim its pre-1949 communist revolution mantle as Asia's financial and cultural hub.

The city's history as an international entrepot and the preponderance of European architecture, as well as its reputation for cultural sophistication, earned it the pre-revolution sobriquet as the Paris of the East.
